messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Fwd: [stan-users] Estimating means of two multi variate normals
parts:
On 11/9/12 4:53 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> It seems that we do not check if the dimension of data declared in the model is the same with that in the data passed in.
> In this example, essentially, the data declared in the model is [2, M], but the real data have dimension [M, 2].

That's bad. In fact, it's even worse than it looks.
It's another place we could seg fault because we're not
really checking the dimensions at all. Here's what the code
geneated for a matrix[3,2] declaration looks like:

m = matrix_d(3,2);
if (!context__.contains_r("m"))
throw std::runtime_error("variable m not found.");
vals_r__ = context__.vals_r("m");
pos__ = 0;
size_t m_m_mat_lim__ = 3;
size_t m_n_mat_lim__ = 2;
for (size_t n_mat__ = 0; n_mat__ < m_n_mat_lim__; ++n_mat__) {
for (size_t m_mat__ = 0; m_mat__ < m_m_mat_lim__; ++m_mat__) {
m(m_mat__,n_mat__) = vals_r__[pos__++];
}
}

So we check the variable exists, but not any of the sizes!

We have all the info we need in the compiled
model (dims of declaration in Stan model and
the dims read from the dump file).

I'll fix it for both Stan and RStan (the fix will either
go in the generated code or in the var_context). Shouldn't
take too long either way.

Somewhere along the line (probably when I added definedness
checks), the constraint checks on transformed params got lost.
I just put them back in.

Then I need to talk to Daniel about adding tests for
models that fail for runtime reasons like bounds checking.
That way, this should help me avoid borking the error checking
in the future.

With all of this and the fact that I also inadvertently bypassed
line/column location reporting for parser errors, we should do
a 1.0.4 patch release ASAP.

- Bob
